verdict.rationale: Letta's own Mods feature lets the agent add "event hooks" to its runtime, which is a first-party mechanism for running actions automatically on events. The Agent SDK's dreaming trigger is a narrow built-in rule that fires memory consolidation on step counts or context compaction. Scheduled tasks are time-based, not event-based, so they are not counted. Mods are trusted code with only a one-line mention, so the depth of user-defined rules is unproven. Missing for 10: documented event types and hook configuration, a no-code rules/trigger UI, examples of event→action rules beyond memory dreaming, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Mods let your agent modify its own runtime — adding tools, commands, event hooks, permission policies, and provider adapters that take effect immediately on reload.
trigger controls when dreaming runs: after a number of steps, on context compaction, or never.
